:
  Allow calls based on contact prefix matching, ideal for organizations using sequential numbers, e.g., clinics or law firms.

This regex must end with dots, in this regex mode, these trailing dots represent the variable digits.

For example:
  .*..
  It matches any contact with the same prefix, allowing for a 2-digit variation at the end.
  If you have 111122 saved as a contact, a call from 111133 will also be allowed.

Another example:
  (?!(04|03))\d{5}..
Breakdown:
  - (?!(03|04))
  Exclude numbers starting with 03 or 04
  - \d{5}
  The number should be 7 digits in total, including the 2-digit variable suffix
  - ..
  2-digit variable suffix

Match contacts by prefix, allowing for variation in the last 2 digits, ideal for organizations using sequential numbers, e.g., clinics or law firms.

For example:
  If you have 11111122 saved as a contact, a call from 11111133 will also be allowed.

Show caller ID in a floating window.

Drag to move it.

Note
You might notice a system alert appears in your notification shade while the floating window is active, indicating this app is displaying window over other apps. That\'s because the floating window has been historically abused by malware to draw fake login screens.
Just ignore this alert, it will vanish along with the floating window.

The content displayed in the caller ID window, in HTML format.

A dash (-) is displayed if the value is empty, for example, when there is no carrier information for the number.
Supported tags:
- {reason}
  Why the call was allowed, same as displayed in call history.
- {number}
  The incoming phone number.
- {contact}
  Contact or caller display name, when available.
- {geolocation}
  The number\'s geolocation.
- {carrier}
  The number\'s carrier name.

Supported HTML tags:
See: link
0: no timer. 1–600: hide after this many seconds. Always hides at call end.
Keeps the existing window after answer until the timer expires or the call ends. Default: off.
Applies when Contacts permission is granted and the caller is found in your address book.

Delay N seconds.

Use case:
For the feature SMS Alert, messages sometimes arrive simultaneously with or a few seconds after a call, adding a 2~3 second call screening delay can prevent such issues.

Extract the comment from the query result for displaying in the notification and history log. (optional)

For example, for this query result:
{
  \"type\": \"MARKETING\",
  \"comment\": \"Better call Saul\",
  …
}

Extract it with:
  \"comment\": \"(.+?)\"

:
  The regex applies to the number\'s carrier name.

Note
  Carrier information is based on the initial registration and may be inaccurate if the number has been transferred (ported).

For example:
  Block numbers from Verizon Wireless with regex verizon.*
Off by default. Only works when Android provides outgoing call details. End-of-call cleanup still applies.
Invalid JSON or options. Use up to 6 unique source IDs, HTTPS URLs, GET/POST and 250–5000 ms timeout.

Online sources are off by default. Enabled sources receive unfamiliar phone numbers, not address-book contacts. Lookup only displays identity and never blocks calls. CallerInfo legacy custom APIs are supported with tel/key parameters, result.* fields, and error_code=0. Templates accept {number} (E.164), {domestic}, and shared_pref(baidu_api_key/juhe_api_key/tmini_api_key) values. Sources merge in JSON order. Tmini is charged per successful call; the phone number and key are sent over HTTPS, but storing the key on a client device risks extraction. A user-owned server proxy is safer. Tencent, 360, and Dianhua still require verified docs and authorization.

This policy applies to general identity cache. Successful Tmini results, including unmarked numbers, are kept permanently in marked.db without automatic expiry or eviction to reduce paid requests. Use Clear cache to remove them manually. API errors are never cached as unmarked.
Save first. Test sends the entered number to saved, enabled sources. Results may be cached. No mark does not mean safe.
Spaces and hyphens are accepted. The local prefix database is checked first, followed by enabled sources. Lookup never blocks a call by itself.
A rule for this number already exists. Check Number Rules.
Removes the prefix only when it is followed by a complete 11-digit mobile number. When off, lookup uses the original number.
Only applies after you add it. It may block legitimate company support or callback numbers; enable only if this suits your needs.
Only applies after you add it. 95/96 numbers may belong to banks, government, or business services; use caution.
Skip online lookup for number prefixes
Load Tmini paid aggregate marking API
New Tmini API loaded and enabled. Successful lookups consume credits per Tmini policy.
New Tmini API loaded but disabled. Enter your key, then load it again.
Loaded and enabled. Queries send numbers to Juhe Data; verify with the test query.
Endpoint and parameters loaded but not enabled. Enter a Juhe API key, then tap this button again.
Default width is the screen width. Set 220–1000 dp; height supports 120–500 dp. Zero height wraps content but never exceeds 500 dp; excess content scrolls.
Preferred source ID (-1 uses list order)
API keys are kept in local preferences and excluded from app configuration backups. The Tmini key is still exposed to client-device extraction risk. Do not put keys directly in exported source JSON.
